requirements.title: Login with valid credentials issues a JWT and lands the user on `/dashboard`.
Login with invalid credentials shows a generic error and stays on `/login`.
Protected routes redirect unauthenticated visitors to `/login` and wrong-role visitors to `/dashboard`.
Logout clears the client session (`token`/`user`) and returns to `/login`.
The login form enforces required Username and Password fields before submission.
A visitor or member can search the public catalog and see matching books.
Book availability (copies and loan state) is exposed consistently on the book detail page and the copies API.
Book detail shows metadata, copies, and the reserve entry point for an authenticated member.
A member can hold at most 3 active loans; a 4th checkout is rejected.
A loan is due 21 days after checkout.
A loan can be renewed once, and renewal is blocked while a PENDING reservation exists.
Staff can return a loan by copy (`POST /api/return` takes the copy id).

An authenticated member can self-checkout by scanning a barcode, bound to the authenticated principal; self-return (`/api/return/scan`) accepts any barcode without a principal check — recorded as a product gap and asserted as-is.
A member can view current loans (`/api/checkout/my`) and checkout history.
A member can reserve an unavailable book; duplicate reservations are rejected.

Reservations carry a FIFO queue position, but `markReady` enforces only PENDING status — a front-of-queue gate and automatic allocation are not implemented, and staff can mark any pending reservation ready.
A pending reservation expires after 7 days and a ready hold after 3 days, per the documented (unswept) policy.
A member can cancel their own reservation (cancel is owner-only); staff can mark a reservation ready and fulfill it.
ADMIN/LIBRARIAN can create and update books.
ADMIN/LIBRARIAN can add copies to a book.
ADMIN/LIBRARIAN can transfer copies between branches.
A book QR code is available through `/api/books/{id}/qr`.
An ADMIN can create users with a role and optional branch, and the created account can log in.
An ADMIN can list, search, and update users, including role and status changes.
An authenticated user can view and update their own profile and change their own password.
An ADMIN can create, update, and delete branches; branch deletion cascades copies (tests never delete branches).
Branch listing and detail are available to authenticated users.
An ADMIN can query the append-only audit trail by entity type and limit.

An expired or invalid token is rejected by the API (HTTP 403 under the current security configuration, which has no 401 authentication entry point); the client's 401-only interceptor does not redirect, so the failure surfaces as an error in the page.
API calls require a valid bearer token; missing or invalid tokens are rejected without granting access (HTTP 403 under the current security configuration).
Role-based access rules are enforced in the UI (navigation, pages, controls) and by the API, including direct navigation to a forbidden route.
`/checkout-desk` is ADMIN-only in the sidebar while its route guard is authentication-only; the current behavior is asserted as-is.
User-visible outcomes of core flows (login, catalog, circulation, reservations, administration) match the redesigned UI described in this spec.
Navigation exposes only the sections the current role can use.
